html:
SMTO-ART-0008 — These files are too large or too many for SMTO to save

GUID: 1202a5ee-4159-43b4-b51e-14e7dc7f69ba
Slug: artifact-size-limit
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • SMTO limits how big and how many saved files a Task can keep or download at once. This file, Task or download went over one of those limits, so it wasn't saved or downloaded.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If Download all failed, open Artifacts from this run and select Download for each file you need instead. Download all has its own size limit, but each file can still be downloaded on its own.
  2. If a file wasn't saved, ask SMTO in a new message to make it smaller, for example by compressing it or splitting it into parts under 64 MB. By default, a single saved file can be at most 64 MB.
  3. If the Task makes many files, ask SMTO to combine them or keep only the ones you need. By default a Task can save up to 200 files and 512 MB in total, and its output folder can hold at most 20,000 items.
  4. If you regularly need bigger outputs, ask the person who manages SMTO whether the file limits can be raised. These limits are set by whoever runs the SMTO server and apply to every Task.

What success looks like

  • The smaller files appear in Artifacts from this run, or each file downloads on its own.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; the details say which limit was reached. Don't delete other saved files or Task history just to make room.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An artifact limit was exceeded: per-file size, per-run byte or file-count quota, ZIP export size, discovery depth (32) or entry (20,000) bounds, temp staging quota, or the 1 MiB Gateway artifact-operation response limit.

What this means

  • Artifact file/run/export limits, discovery depth/entry bounds or bounded transport-response size are exceeded. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Artifact file/run/export limits, discovery depth/entry bounds or bounded transport-response size are exceeded.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the actual enforced bound before reducing files; encoded response and directory traversal limits differ from file bytes.

How to fix it

  • Read the diagnostic to see which limit tripped. Limits come from ArtifactLimits (AOR_ARTIFACT_MAX_FILE_BYTES default 64 MiB, AOR_ARTIFACT_MAX_RUN_BYTES 512 MiB, AOR_ARTIFACT_MAX_RUN_COUNT 200, AOR_ARTIFACT_MAX_EXPORT_BYTES 512 MiB) or the artifact_limits setting, plus fixed discovery bounds in gateway_core/artifact_discovery.py; raise a limit deliberately or have the task produce fewer or smaller outputs.
  • Reduce or split the artifact or export while preserving complete bytes and intended outputs.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Deliberately scoped complete outputs fit all applicable publication/export bounds.

What not to do

  • Do not erase authoritative receipts or protected current input to conceal a size/capacity problem.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
